source_text: Οὐδεμία ἀνάγκη τοῖς νοῦν ἔχουσιν, ἐξ ὧν μετὰ τὸ βάπτισμα ὁ Χριστὸς ἔπραξε, παριστᾶν τὸ ἀληθὲς καὶ ἀφανταστὸν τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῦ σώματος, τῆς καθ' ἡμᾶς ἀνθρωπίνης φύσεως. Τὰ γὰρ μετὰ τὸ βάπτισμα ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ πραχθέντα, καὶ μάλιστα τὰ σημεῖα, τὴν αὐτοῦ κεκρυμμένην ἐν σαρκὶ θεότητα ἐδήλουν, καὶ ἐπιστοῦντο τῷ κόσμῳ. Θεὸς γὰρ ὢν ὁμοῦ τε καὶ ἄνθρωπος τέλειος ὁ αὐτὸς τὰς δύο αὐτοῦ οὐσίας ἐπιστώσατο ἡμῖν, τὴν μὲν θεότητα αὐτοῦ διὰ τῶν σημείων ἐν τῇ τριετίᾳ τῇ μετὰ τὸ βάπτισμα, τὴν δὲ ἀνθρωπότητα αὐτοῦ ἐν τοῖς τριάκοντα χρόνοις τοῖς πρὸ τοῦ βαπτίσματος, ἐν οἷς διὰ τὸ ἀτελὲς τὸ κατὰ σάρκα ἀπέκρυβε τὰ σημεῖα τῆς αὐτοῦ θεότητος, καίπερ θεὸς ἀληθὴς προαιώνιος ὑπάρχων.
pass_a_gloss: No necessity to those having mind, from which things after the baptism Christ did, to show the true and invisible of his soul and body, of the human nature according to us. For the things after the baptism done by Christ, and especially the signs, showed his deity hidden in flesh, and were convincing to the world. For being God and also perfect man the same one guaranteed to us his two substances, the one his deity through the signs in the three years after the baptism, and the other his humanity in the thirty years before the baptism, in which because of the imperfection according to flesh he hid the signs of his deity, although being true and pre-existent God.

choices.why: best fit for the context of confirming or establishing something
accurate translation of the Greek word

pass_b_english: Those who have understanding need no proof drawn from what Christ did after his baptism to demonstrate the true and invisible reality of his soul and body, of our human nature. For the works he performed after his baptism, and especially the signs, revealed his deity hidden in flesh and convinced the world. Since he was God and perfect man together, the same one confirmed to us his two natures: his deity through the signs during the three years after his baptism, and his humanity during the thirty years before his baptism, when, because of the imperfection belonging to the flesh, he concealed the signs of his deity, even though he existed as the true, pre‑existent God.

review.notes: Pass A and Pass B both accurately reflect the Greek text. Pass B provides a more fluent rendering of the first clause 'Οὐδεμία ἀνάγκη τοῖς νοῦν ἔχουσιν' (No necessity to those having mind) as 'Those who have understanding need no proof'. The distinction between 'substances' (Pass A) and 'natures' (Pass B) for 'οὐσίας' is acceptable in a patristic context. The translation of 'ἐπιστώσατο' as 'guaranteed' (Pass A) and 'confirmed' (Pass B) is faithful to the Greek.
